about: The homepage hero's opening (Nov 11, 2026; CLAUDE.md section 3). Robert's photos flick through as tiles (his face first: it is also the largest tile on a wide screen, so the page's largest paint is the opening's first frame) on the hero's own tar ground, the count runs up on a pink plate, then the hero's picture cuts in and the screen rests. Times are seconds from the start; the whole run ends inside five seconds on purpose (WCAG 2.2.2: nothing to pause, so no button), and no more than three tiles change in any one second (WCAG 2.3.1). Where a tile goes: 'phone' (phones and portrait screens) is either the strip, the room between the header and the mark, with a box of [left, top, width, height] in percent of it, or the side, the room to the right of the mark (from the top of the strip to the foot of the mark), which the tile fills across, standing on the mark's foot, as tall as the room or 'k' times its width; the card's 'side' is its photo beside the mark when the strip is too short for a photo over the plate; 'wide' (landscape, 760 and up) is a box in percent of the stage to the right of the words. 'pos' is the crop's object-position; 'crop' ([left, top, right, bottom] as fractions of the cleared copy) cuts a band first for a tile that is shown wide, so its pixels go where they show; 'px' is the long side written and 'q' the WebP quality. Every photo is a registry photo (scripts/photos.js), read from its cleared copy in cfc-site/img/ph/. python3 tools/hero-open.py writes the tiles; node scripts/build-home.js writes the markup; tools/test/hero-open.test.js holds the rules. A changed tile gets a new number ('n').
